artifacts.summary: Implementation summary covering all five phases: eight --task wiring sites, five inapplicability records, the carve-out ruling, the live exit-3 demonstration, and the deploy/verify gate run with two reasoned exclusions.

completion_data.completion_summary: Wired --task {N} at every single-task commit-staging recipe site, recorded inapplicability reasons at the remaining sites, recorded the task-scoped-directory carve-out ruling in git-staging-scope.md, and proved a live exit-3 refusal with a positive control. Deployed and verified; two reasoned exclusions traced to a concurrent sibling task's in-flight manifest.json wiring, outside this task's file_scope.

memory_candidates.content: When wiring a new opt-in flag onto an existing, already-correctly-wired sibling flag (e.g. --task beside --honest-index-rows), re-grep the full site inventory at implementation time rather than trusting a research/plan-time count -- a plan-time re-grep can itself surface a surprise site (e.g. a pseudo-code Execution Flow line one level up from the documented examples) that the original research table predates. Rule on it explicitly rather than skipping it because it postdates the table.

To prove a contended-path/lease-style refusal mechanism live rather than merely present in text, build a throwaway scratch git repo mirroring the primitive's own test suite fixture shape (copy the script plus its runtime deps, write the same manifest/claim files), run the exact recipe argv against a pre-claimed path, and pair the refusal assertion with a --flag-omitted positive control on the identical fixture -- the positive control is what proves the refusal was caused by the flag rather than an unrelated precondition.
